project.title: Williamstown Theatre Festival 2025
project.maker: Pentagram (Andrea Trabucco-Campos and team) for Williamstown Theatre Festival
project.medium: festival visual identity and performance key-visual system

why: A clear reference for keeping a festival identity recognizable while changing its yearly art direction: one blur behavior gives distinct performance images a shared sense of motion across print, environmental, and digital formats.

compositions.title: Motion frozen into each performance image
compositions.study: Pentagram applies a blur motion behavior to photography and typography, then uses a distinct key image to convey each performance.
compositions.reuse: Define one transformation rule that can make varied subjects feel like a coherent event season without forcing them into one repeated picture.

compositions.title: A key visual that scales through the festival ecosystem
compositions.study: The system extends from performance key visuals to signage, wayfinding, programme design, badges, digital billboards, social media, and merchandise.
compositions.reuse: Treat the poster composition as a portable rule set, then test its hierarchy at close-reading, streetscape, and scrolling scales.

assets.notes: The source documents key images for individual performances; no source photography is copied into this library.
assets.reuse: Use original or licensed imagery with an equivalent movement treatment rather than reusing campaign photography.

assets.notes: The case study identifies Review Condensed and Times New Roman as the bold-and-evergreen type pairing.
assets.reuse: Pair a high-impact condensed face with a quieter text face when changing art direction still needs a stable information voice.

assets.notes: The 2025 expression retains the Williamstown monogram and dynamic-stages graphic system established for the prior edition.
assets.reuse: Keep a small core of durable marks or graphics fixed while letting the annual image treatment evolve.

motion.title: Blur as a system-level movement rule
motion.study: Photography and typography share blur as a visual behavior; Pentagram describes animated key images made with Runway and AfterEffects.
motion.reuse: Use a restrained, accessible motion treatment that also reads as a strong static frame; provide a still alternative when motion is unavailable.

implementation.format: Festival poster/key-visual system with a shared blur behavior and stable identity foundation
implementation.notes: The official Pentagram case study documents the project context, design behavior, system applications, typography, and credits. This entry records reusable principles only; all source artwork, photography, typefaces, and motion assets remain external.
